modelSource: Opus selected by the launcher; the session reports model ID claude-opus-5-5. Model review is not human review.
reviewStatusNote: All 120 rows (60 es-en, 60 en-es) are present and were read in full: objective, focus, speaking card, opening line, grammar, every aligned sentence, every term and phrase, and every verb. Corrections were applied where needed and re-validated. This status covers source review and correction only; runtime integration, HD audio, offline packs and human-qualified review are separate and not done here.

files.notEdited: No runtime, shared, test, script or other-module files were changed. git was not run.

countsNote: Ranges are min-max per stage. Foundation/Core: 5-9 sentences, 8-12 terms, 4-6 phrases, 3-5 verbs. Master: 12-18 sentences, 12-16 terms, 6-8 phrases, exactly 5 verbs. lesson.words and content.words are identical in every row.

severityScale.P0: Wrong money arithmetic that teaches a false financial fact.
severityScale.P1: Wrong meaning, contradictory or reversed scene, misleading grammar rule, false friend, wrong financial treatment, or missing/invented jurisdiction.
severityScale.P2: Lesson objective not met by the scene, unquantified case, terminology or regional mismatch.

summary.lessonsWithoutLoggedCorrection: Only en-es Foundation 10, which was read in full and needed no change; every other lesson has at least one logged correction. Module-wide sweep fixes (Let's, accented names) are listed under moduleWideFindings.
recurringProblemsFixed: Reversed or wrong speakers: creditor promising to pay (Core 6), owner approving his own payment run (Core 7), bank officer asking which documents the bank needs (Core 18), client asking the accountant whether she understood (Master 14), learner asking the trainer for the teach-back (Master 19), accountant telling the client not to record an entry the accountant records (Master 17), bank opening lines written as the caller (Core 21).

Arithmetic and financial logic: a 200 tax credit called worth more than a deduction that saves 200 (Core 23, both pairs); bank reconciliations whose items could not balance (Core 8, Master 1); unquantified profit, cash, variance, budget and loan cases (Core 12-16, 19; Master 10, 18, 20).

Financial terminology: pending hold versus settled charge (Foundation 7), double entry misstated as debit or credit (Foundation 8), receivable confirmed with the supplier (Foundation 6), foreign invoices converted only at the payment-date rate (Core 26), sender fee confused with amount received (Master 15), the whole loan treated as current (Core 13).

Jurisdiction: the invented country Norland/Norlandia replaced by real named contexts with fictional figures: Spain (IRPF, pago fraccionado, Agencia Tributaria, propuesta de liquidación) in es-en; United States (federal return, Form W-2, 1099-INT, 1099-NEC, 1099-B, estimated payments, IRS CP2000) in en-es; es-en Core 23 uses a US federal example to teach that Spain's IRPF uses deducción differently. Unlabeled tax deadlines were replaced with internal or bank deadlines; no live rates or universal benefits are asserted.

Spanish grammar notes: ser/estar as permanent/temporary, ayudar with obligatory le, no sé si with subjunctive, quisiera called conditional, repartir and convertir stem changes, deberse a agreement, passive se called reflexive, pagar/cargar/clasificar 'no spelling change', ungrammatical tanto como comparatives.
False friend: error material (a clerical slip in Spanish) glossed as material error in both directions; replaced with error significativo.

English-specific grammar in en-es: stative owe in past continuous (was owing), work for her own account (calque), a proof of payment, Assets equals as the singular rule, equal to as the verb pattern, due to called a noun, would plus unless plus present, would-if-present mixes, take responsibility for for task assignment, exceed called a noun, keep to hand in a US scene, take a decision in a US track, Let us for suggestions, Mr. plus first name, English sentences inside Spanish-native notes.
Register: tú between coworkers and usted with clients made consistent; near-future Spanish presents translated with will.

findings.explanation: Spanish said traer al banco (bring to the bank) but English said bring from the bank; the client is bringing bank records to the accountant.
findings.correction: Rewrote as le recuerdo qué documentos del banco debe traer / remind you which bank documents to bring.

findings.explanation: Taught ser/estar as permanent versus temporary, which is misleading as a rule.
findings.correction: Reframed as identity/profession/category versus location/current state.

findings.explanation: Ayudar note claimed helping a person always takes indirect le/les; ayudar is transitive (lo/la), with le as accepted leísmo, especially with usted.
findings.correction: Rewrote the verb note and phrase note; changed the example to Ayudo a mis clientes con los impuestos.

findings.explanation: The client chose a video call, then the assistant told him to bring receipts in person; contact details were never confirmed.
findings.correction: Rewrote the scene: video format, documents sent by email before Monday, contact address corrected, and closure with the confirmed time.

findings.explanation: The scene named the documents but never stated how an invoice and a receipt differ, which is the lesson outcome.
findings.correction: Sentence 6 now contrasts invoice (requests payment) with receipt (shows payment made).

findings.explanation: The revisar example was an odd statement with an inverted subject, and its note contradicted it.
findings.correction: Turned it into a question and rewrote the note.

findings.explanation: Presented the decimal comma as Spanish-wide; Mexico and much of Central America use a decimal point. The reading of 1.250,50 as fifty hundredths was unnatural.
findings.correction: Rewrote the note with the regional formats.

findings.explanation: The client said January to March and the accountant answered No with the same period. A tax due date was asserted with no jurisdiction.
findings.correction: The client now guesses the whole year; the date is the firm's internal deadline, so no unlabeled tax deadline is asserted.

findings.explanation: Money owed to the bakery was to be confirmed with the supplier; a receivable is collected from the customer.
findings.correction: The pending collection is now an unpaid customer invoice confirmed with that customer.

findings.explanation: Said pagar has no spelling change; it has pagué/pague.
findings.correction: Corrected the note.

findings.explanation: The pending hold was called a charge the bank had not confirmed, and the closing line mentioned a fee that never existed.
findings.correction: Made it a pending card hold not yet settled; the closing line records the pending charge; fixed de los que parecen.

findings.explanation: Described tengo as an e-to-ie stem change.
findings.correction: Corrected the irregularity description.

findings.explanation: Said each purchase is a debit or credit depending on the account (double entry has both), and debe pagar had the bank as its subject.
findings.correction: Each purchase now has a debit and a credit, with a worked credit card example; the cardholder repays.

findings.explanation: Cerrar el plazo de marzo is unidiomatic; several near-future Spanish presents were rendered as I send.
findings.correction: Rewrote to cerrar el mes de marzo; translations use will; added an identifying detail (invoice number).

findings.explanation: A near-future Spanish present was translated as I send it tomorrow; the grammar note ignored the Spain preference for he recibido with hoy; the acordar note was vague.
findings.correction: Translated with will, added the regional preterite/perfect note, and clarified the acordar stem change and acordarse de.

findings.explanation: The scene requested records but never limited the set, although the lesson teaches a scoped request with solo.
findings.correction: Sentence 5 now scopes the invoices with solo and defers payroll.

findings.explanation: English translations used Let us for suggestions in 7 es-en lessons (es-en/core/1, es-en/core/14, es-en/core/4, es-en/master/1, es-en/master/10, es-en/master/5, es-en/master/6); in modern English Let us is formal or means allow us.
findings.correction: Replaced with Let's in English translations; a parallel global pass fixed English target text in en-es (Let us to Let's; accented names Julián, Iván, Verónica).

findings.explanation: The por example Pagamos el horno por una cantidad fija was unnatural Spanish and did not illustrate exchange clearly.
findings.correction: Replaced with Pagamos 4.500 euros por el horno in the reading, grammar and phrase list; fixed the clasificar spelling-change note.

findings.explanation: Coworkers addressed each other with usted commands and an usted opening, which is stiff for a team review.
findings.correction: Switched the coworker lines to tú and noted the usted form for clients.

findings.explanation: The collection was called Tuesday's and then said to arrive Monday, and the 1,200 movement was never stated. The pagar example was copied from another lesson.
findings.correction: Clarified arrival versus recording date, stated the amount and gave a lesson-specific example.

findings.explanation: A value date later than the invoice date was presented as a discrepancy, which is normal; the opening line contradicted the scene's direction.
findings.correction: The reference is the mismatch; the value date explains why the payment was not matched automatically; the closure applies the payment to the invoice.

findings.explanation: The collector said pagaremos (we will pay) for the client, and the client's hoped-for Friday payment contradicted the Monday commitment.
findings.correction: Rewrote the exchange: the accountant proposes with subjunctive, the client commits to Monday, and the closure sets a written follow-up.

findings.explanation: The owner, who approves, told the bookkeeper we will pay when you approve; only two of the three bills were reviewed; the Mexican corrida de pagos conflicted with the lesson term lote de pagos.
findings.correction: Rewrote the scene with the correct speakers, all three bills, and a closure stating which bills enter the payment run.

findings.explanation: The scene said the whole difference was due to two checks, then added a deposit in transit and a fee with no figures, so the reconciliation could not balance. The deberse a note claimed agreement with the cause.
findings.correction: Rebuilt with figures: 9,000 - 900 - 600 + 400 = 7,900 and 7,930 - 30 = 7,900; corrected the agreement rule.

findings.explanation: The pluperfect sentence had no prior reference point, después de que llegara is nonstandard for a past fact, and the question in the preterite was answered in the present.
findings.correction: Anchored the pluperfect to the statement's arrival, simplified the detection sentence, aligned tenses and stated the reversal amount.

findings.explanation: Payroll deductions had no jurisdiction and mixed Latin American aportes with a euro payslip; net pay was compared with an unexplained previous year; focus called passive se reflexive.
findings.correction: Labeled the fictional payslip as from Spain with cotizaciones and IRPF withholding (no rates), stated 1,200 - 260 = 940, and corrected the focus and grammar note.

findings.explanation: Objective required a labeled jurisdiction but none was named; asked whether she was autónoma or por cuenta propia (the same thing); taught ser as permanent; implied the contract alone decides classification; no next review step.
findings.correction: Set the case in Madrid, Spain; fixed the question; framed review as contract versus actual working arrangement; requested payslips conditionally; added a specialist review step.

findings.explanation: Taught ungrammatical comparisons: La utilidad no es tanto como esperábamos and las ventas netas son tanto como las del mes anterior; no figures for revenue, expenses or profit.
findings.correction: Rebuilt the comparatives (mayor/menor que, tan ... como, verb + tanto como) and added 42,000 - 36,500 = 5,500.

findings.explanation: The whole loan was called a current liability; no figures supported the equation; English grammar errors (What does the current assets include).
findings.correction: Only the portion due this year is current; added 80,000 = 30,000 + 50,000; fixed English agreement and the tener note.

findings.explanation: No figures connected the profit, the uncollected sale and the payment, and the owner never repeated the distinction.
findings.correction: Added the 3,000 profit, 7,500 receivable and 4,200 payment, plus a teach-back closure.

findings.explanation: Variable costs had no figure, so affordability could not be discussed; the euro setting used Latin American camioneta; the grammar note allowed the conditional in a real condition.
findings.correction: Added variable costs and the 18,000 - 6,500 - 3,000 = 8,500 margin; used furgoneta with a regional note; corrected the si-clause rule.

findings.explanation: The planned and actual amounts were never stated, the variance was asked about for the quarter in a monthly review, and there was no corrective step.
findings.correction: Added 3,300 - 2,400 = 900, fixed the period and added the agreed corrective step.

findings.explanation: The client asked the accountant to confirm the invoice, though the open question needed the client's answer; the update never asked the client to confirm or correct it.
findings.correction: The accountant now asks the client to answer the open question by the deadline; the client confirms and offers corrections.

findings.explanation: The bank officer asked the client which documents the bank needs, the client answered, and the closing implied approval; funcionario means civil servant in Spain; quisiera was called a conditional.
findings.correction: The client asks and the banker lists documents; the closing sets delivery and the next meeting without implying approval; fixed the quisiera note.

findings.explanation: The repartir note claimed an e-to-ie stem change; repartir is regular.
findings.correction: Corrected the note.

findings.explanation: The quote had no rate or payment figure, so the 4,100 total was unsupported; the grammar taught un interés de 8 por ciento por año.
findings.correction: Built a consistent fictional quote: 20,000 at 6% for 60 months is about 387 a month, about 3,200 interest, a 200 fee, about 3,400 total cost; rates now use anual.

findings.explanation: A bank employee was called a prestamista (money lender); the reason for a personal guarantee was unclear; secured guarantee is not idiomatic English.
findings.correction: Recast the roles, made the aval depend on the valuation falling short, and translated garantía real as collateral.

findings.explanation: The bank officer's opening line said Llamo por una comisión, which is the caller's line; the trigger sentence said the minimum balance fell rather than the balance fell below the minimum.
findings.correction: Rewrote the opening line as the bank answering, fixed the trigger and the follow-up logic, and used future forms for the bank's stated next step.

findings.explanation: Used the invented country Norlandia; the preliminary review asked for a real named context with fictional figures.
findings.correction: Set the meeting in Spain (declaración de la renta, certificado de retenciones, Agencia Tributaria) with no dates or rates asserted.

findings.explanation: A 1,000 deduction at 20% saves 200, and a 200 credit was then said to be worth more than it; both save 200.
findings.correction: Compared equal 1,000 amounts: the deduction saves 200, the credit 1,000.

findings.explanation: Used invented Norlandia; the focus named a nonexistent de ... que comparative; did not warn that Spain's IRPF uses deducción for a credit against the tax and reducción for base reductions.
findings.correction: Set on a US federal return with fictional figures, used crédito tributario, added the Spain terminology note, corrected the comparative focus and closed without a universal benefit claim.

findings.explanation: An autónomo (Spain) was told the final calculation happens in December, with no jurisdiction named; in Spain the IRPF year is settled in the following year's return.
findings.correction: Labeled the case as Spain, used pago fraccionado / pago a cuenta / declaración anual, and explained the settlement without dates or rates.

findings.explanation: Valor de costo is not standard Spanish for cost basis, and the capital-gain question had no jurisdiction.
findings.correction: Used valor de adquisición and the broker's informe fiscal, and named Spain's IRPF label ganancia patrimonial.

findings.explanation: Taught converting a foreign invoice only at the payment-date rate, not the invoice date; under accrual accounting the invoice uses the transaction-date rate and the payment difference is an exchange difference. The convertir note said o to ue and exceeded 160 characters; the revisa example was labeled an usted command.
findings.correction: Rewrote the scene with invoice-date and payment-date rates and the exchange difference, made the specialist question concrete, closed on who sends the figure, and fixed the verb notes.

findings.explanation: Tú prepara el registro mixed a command with a stated subject; only two of three requested items were assigned; the pedir note exceeded 160 characters.
findings.correction: Used tú preparas, assigned all three items, added the teach-back confirmation and shortened the note.

findings.explanation: Mixed usted (le dejo) and tú (avísame) between the same colleagues.
findings.correction: Made the colleague register consistently tú.

findings.explanation: The call ended with No hay problema and no secure route for documents; the compartir note was garbled.
findings.correction: Added a callback on the official number and the approved portal route; fixed the note.

findings.explanation: The cerrar note exceeded 160 characters, and the enviar note claimed nosotros keeps the stress on the stem.
findings.correction: Shortened and corrected both notes.

findings.explanation: The first explanation and the remaining gap were never quantified, so the revision of the reconciliation was not traceable; the closing review was noted before the evidence.
findings.correction: Added the first explanation (236 - 150 = 86), the 86-euro charge as the missing item, the evidence request and the documented revision.

findings.explanation: A partial payment added twice was offered to explain an invoice that was lower than the statement, the credit-note question was unanswered, and the accountant said yo decido.
findings.correction: Made the 300-euro gap a possible duplicated delivery charge, requested all three source documents, and made the source document decide the figure.

findings.explanation: An unlabeled tax filing was given a partial version and an extension, which depend on jurisdiction; the grammar paired the conditional with si plus the present indicative.
findings.correction: Made the deadline a bank submission under a loan agreement, used a provisional version and a bank extension request, and taught si plus imperfect subjunctive with the conditional.

findings.explanation: Error material was glossed as material error; in Spanish it normally means a clerical slip, and the significant-error sense is error significativo or de importancia relativa.
findings.correction: Replaced the term with error significativo and added a note on the false friend.

findings.explanation: Taught that no sé si takes the subjunctive; it takes the indicative (the example itself used será). Eso es el efecto should be Ese es el efecto.
findings.correction: Taught es posible que plus subjunctive versus no sé si plus indicative; fixed the demonstrative; added a concrete 12,400 versus 1,240 error.

findings.explanation: A tax notice had no jurisdiction; requerimiento (request for documents) was paired with a claimed amount; cuota was glossed as installment in a tax context; the client told the adviser to keep the documents to hand.
findings.correction: Set in Spain with a propuesta de liquidación, importe propuesto and the reply period; glossed cuota as tax amount due; corrected the speakers; added a teach-back closure.

findings.explanation: Said the lease returns the residual value (lo devolvemos) instead of the van; maintenance and depreciation were contrasted vaguely; costs had no figures; tasa de interés real could mean the inflation-adjusted rate.
findings.correction: Stated an example cost gap, tied depreciation to ownership and maintenance to lease terms, mentioned a purchase option and referred to the bank offer's rate.

findings.explanation: A self-employed worker was told the adjustment happens at year end with no jurisdiction; March income was said to invalidate an April payment that should already have included it.
findings.correction: Set in Spain (Málaga, under the Agencia Tributaria rather than a foral regime), moved the new income to May, kept the April Q1 payment valid, and settled the year in the annual return.

findings.explanation: The discrepancy had no cause, so the master complication was missing; the note said reflexive se shows who approved, when passive se hides the agent.
findings.correction: Added the cause (payroll ran on the pre-approval hours file), clarified the overtime correction and fixed the grammar note.

findings.explanation: Collections (receivables) handled a payment to a vendor; No creo que nos hayan pagado mal contradicted the vendor's claim; the vendor's immediate-resend demand had no double-payment or bank-detail verification step.
findings.correction: Rewrote with the payables team, a changed bank account as the complication, no resend until the trace, a recall request, verification of new account details through the known contact, and a written statement of what remains unverified.

findings.explanation: The shortage was never quantified, the landlord's security deposit was treated as restricted cash in the business's bank, and se queda sin efectivo had no subject.
findings.correction: Built a traceable position: 11,000 in the bank - 3,000 restricted = 8,000 available against 12,000 due (4,000 short), with 14,000 receivables next month and a supplier-terms option that covers the week.

findings.explanation: A mortgage guarantee was delivered rather than signed; the Latin American avalúo appeared in a euro setting; the conditions precedent term was listed but not explained in the scene; the confirmar example was copied from another lesson.
findings.correction: Named both conditions precedent, used firmar la garantía hipotecaria and tasación, used tipo de interés, and gave a lesson-specific example.

findings.explanation: Mixed ustedes verbs with le for one client; the delivery timing question was answered with a quote date; honorario mensual is unidiomatic; the confirmar example came from a bank lesson.
findings.correction: Used usted consistently, answered the delivery timing, used honorarios, and gave a lesson-specific confirmar example.

findings.explanation: Entrega de guardia is a shift handover (usually clinical), not a case handoff; the call ended without the colleague confirming the callback time.
findings.correction: Used traspaso and added a closing commitment with the time and next owner.

findings.explanation: The client asked the accountant ¿Entendió usted la conclusión?, reversing the teach-back; no misunderstanding was corrected; the technical note itself was never read aloud.
findings.correction: Rewrote the scene: the accountant reads the note, translates it into plain language, asks for the explain-back, corrects a provision misunderstanding and confirms the meaning.

findings.explanation: The sender fee was presented as a reason the recipient got less, though a fee charged separately does not reduce the amount received; the currency of receipt and the charge option were never stated.
findings.correction: Separated the 35-euro sender fee (charged separately), the conversion into pesos and a possible intermediary fee under shared charges (SHA), and requested both sides' documents.

findings.explanation: An unnamed authority issued a compliance request, and the reason and approved route were generic; the file-upload problem had no practical answer.
findings.correction: Made it a bank due diligence request on the source of funds, with the bank's portal as the approved route, a practical upload fallback through the official number, and a verification closure.

findings.explanation: The accountant told the client No registre el gasto although the accountant is the one recording it; the client asked the accountant when he could send the receipt; an unlabeled deductibility claim replaced the real issue of classification.
findings.correction: The accountant refuses and explains the missing evidence (expense, advance or loan), records the bank outflow as a pending item, asks the client for the invoice with a date, and gives the client a negative command about the client's own books.

findings.explanation: A tax return deadline of 30 November was stated with no jurisdiction; the cash priority had no available-cash figure; the finance director decided alone; the manager never confirmed the order.

findings.explanation: The new coworker asked the trainer to repeat the steps in his own words (and in usted), so there was no teach-back, and the overlooked check was never overlooked by the learner.

findings.explanation: The conflicting records, the changed estimate and the open item were never specified, so nothing could be reconciled or handed off precisely; the tax impact had no period or jurisdiction.

moduleWideFindings.explanation: en-es mirrored the es-en scenes with dollars but kept Spain-only or jurisdiction-free tax content.
moduleWideFindings.correction: en-es tax, payroll and contractor lessons now use US federal labels and English-specific grammar; es-en uses Spain. Scenes still share characters and storylines by design, but grammar focus, notes and jurisdiction content are authored per target language.

remainingUncertainties: es-en regional standard is mixed: the setting is Spain (euros, nómina, extracto, IRPF, furgoneta) but Latin American terms remain in places (utilidad, costo, monto, cotización, tasa de interés, cuenta de clientes versus cuentas por cobrar). Notes name the variants where they matter; a human editor should choose one default or label each lesson's region.
Haiku's open choices remain for a human decision: contadora versus contable in Spain, cuenta corriente default, céntimo versus centavo, comprobante versus justificante versus recibo.

Spain tax content is stated at a general level and should be checked by a Spain-qualified tax professional: pago fraccionado (modelo 130) applies to many but not all autónomos; propuesta de liquidación with alegaciones describes the limited-review procedure; Málaga, Sevilla, Valencia, Zaragoza and Valladolid were chosen to stay under the common regime (not the Basque or Navarre foral systems).

US tax content uses real form names and periods (Form W-2, 1099-INT, 1099-NEC, 1099-B, estimated payment covering April-May due in June, CP2000 as a proposed-change notice that is not a bill). These were correct to the reviewer's knowledge but can change and should be checked by a US-qualified preparer before release.

Payroll lessons (Core 10) name deduction types (IRPF withholding and Social Security contributions in Spain; federal withholding, Social Security and Medicare in the US) with fictional totals and no rates; the 260 deduction total is illustrative.

Loan quote figures (Core 19) are rounded from a standard amortization (20,000 at 6% for 60 months is about 386.66 a month and about 3,199 interest); TIN/TAE (Spain) and APR (US) notes are definitions, not rates.

Accounting treatments are taught at an introductory level: foreign-currency invoices recorded at the transaction-date rate with an exchange difference on payment; a provision recognized before payment; a replacement oven capitalized as a fixed asset. Firm-specific capitalization thresholds or reporting frameworks are not addressed.
English date style: en-es uses US month-day order; es-en English translations use day-month order (1 January). Both are internally consistent per file but differ between files.
Spanish natives in en-es use a neutral Latin American register (contador, utilidad, cotización, corrida de pagos); a few Spain-leaning words remain (furgoneta in Master 6).
Validator coverage is structural plus term and phrase usage; naturalness of every sentence was judged by the model and should get native-speaker review in both languages.
